key_insight: The paper shows that off-the-shelf image Vision Transformers can learn strong video representations without specialized 3D video models. By turning videos into “super images” and training with masked self-supervision, VideoMSN efficiently captures spatio-temporal information from unlabeled data.
problem_solved: It addresses the high cost and complexity of learning video representations, which often depends on heavy 3D architectures or reconstruction-based autoencoders. The goal is to make self-supervised video learning more efficient using standard image models.
method: Convert each video into a super image: a grid of sampled frames arranged into one image.
Create two complementary views from the super image using spatial patch masking and temporal masking.
Train a Masked Siamese Network with a standard image Vision Transformer to learn spatio-temporal features without labels.
impact: This approach lowers the barrier for practitioners who want scalable video pretraining without building specialized video backbones. It suggests that strong video understanding can be achieved by reusing mature image-model tooling in a simpler and more efficient way.

paper_title: Image Classifiers are Efficient Self-Supervised Video Representation Learners
paper_authors: Owais Iqbal, Sudipta Sarkar, Shyam Marjit, Omprakash Chakraborty, Anirban Chakraborty
